headline: Take-Two Interactive smashed last night after GTA 6 release fears, while Labor doubles down on linking tax cuts to property investor changes — a big week for Aussie politics and your portfolio.

portfolio.summary: A pretty quiet day for ASX holdings — most barely moved at today's close. The action was mostly in US stocks last night, where Take-Two Interactive copped a serious hit, dropping over 4%. Google also slipped about 1.2%. Your ASX ETFs (VDHG, VTS, VGE, CBA, FUEL) were all flat to marginally lower, suggesting the local market is in a bit of a holding pattern.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Dropped $10.53 last night to $227.55 USD — a sharp fall of over 4%. GTA 6 pre-order and release timeline speculation is swirling, and any uncertainty around that game (their biggest ever bet) tends to spook investors. Worth keeping a close eye on any official Rockstar announcements.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Slipped $4.69 last night to $382.97 USD. No major company-specific bad news — the broader tech mood was mixed. Google just announced a new AI model called Gemini Omni (more in the AI section), so the fundamentals story remains intact. The dip looks more like general market rotation than anything structural.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: Fell about 0.9% today to $8.78. Crude oil (WTI) dropped nearly 5% last night to $91.82 USD a barrel — that's a big move for oil. OPEC also cut its global oil demand growth forecast for 2026, which adds more downward pressure on energy stocks. FUEL tracks global energy companies, so cheaper oil directly hurts the fund's value.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: The one bright spot today — up a modest 0.25% to $92.61. The Aussie dollar ticked up slightly (now 71.7 US cents), which can sometimes dampen returns on overseas holdings, but emerging markets held up well regardless.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: Edged down 0.27% to $515.68 today. The US S&P 500 and NASDAQ actually rose last night, but the AUD strengthened slightly, which reduces the value of US-denominated holdings when converted back to Aussie dollars.

movers.name: Commonwealth Bank of Australia
movers.note: Essentially flat — down just 10 cents to $164.50. Nothing to see here today, though the ongoing debate about RBA rate rises (see Politics) is always worth tracking for bank stocks.

markets.summary: US markets finished in the green last night — the S&P 500 up 0.37% and NASDAQ up 0.19% — a decent enough session. The ASX 200 gave back 0.43% today though, closing at 8,654. The big macro story is oil: WTI crude oil crashed nearly 5% last night to under $92 a barrel after OPEC trimmed its demand growth outlook. Gold continued its run higher, up 0.35% to $4,537 USD per ounce. The Aussie dollar is holding firm at 71.7 US cents, slightly stronger than yesterday.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Modest pullback today after recent gains.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session — solid gains led by broad market buying.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night — modest tech gains despite some individual stock weakness.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Big drop last night — OPEC cut its 2026 demand forecast, sending oil sharply lower.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Continues its strong run — investors still seeking safe havens.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar ticking up despite cooling RBA rate hike expectations — global risk appetite is supportive.

politics.summary: It's a big week for economic policy in Australia. Labor is pressing ahead with a plan to link popular income tax cuts to changes affecting property investors, and there's fresh debate about whether the RBA should actually be raising interest rates rather than cutting them. These stories matter directly for your mortgage, investments, and tax bill.

stories.title: Labor ties income tax cuts to CGT and negative gearing changes
stories.why_it_matters: Labor wants to deliver income tax cuts but is tying them to two controversial changes: reducing the capital gains tax (CGT) discount — that's the 50% tax break investors currently get when they sell an asset they've held over a year, which Labor wants to cut — and tightening negative gearing rules on existing investment properties (negative gearing lets landlords deduct rental losses against their income tax). If you own investment property, this hits you directly. The ABC reports Labor is ignoring calls to pause these CGT changes, signalling they're pressing ahead regardless of industry pushback.

stories.title: Expert breaks from consensus and calls for RBA to hike rates
stories.why_it_matters: While most economists expect the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) to be done with rate hikes, at least one expert is publicly calling for more increases. Meanwhile, bond markets are actually moving the other way — the AFR reports that fears of government debt and rate hike bets are unwinding, meaning investors are buying Australian government bonds again (which happens when people expect rates to fall or stay steady). For mortgage holders, this is a mixed signal — the mainstream view is rates are close to their peak, but not everyone agrees.

stories.title: Why is the Aussie dollar rising despite cooling rate hike expectations?
stories.why_it_matters: Normally, if the RBA looks less likely to raise rates, the Aussie dollar would fall (because lower rates make Australian savings less attractive to foreign investors). But the AUD is actually rising right now — sitting at 71.7 US cents. The reason appears to be global: the US dollar is weakening broadly, which lifts most other currencies including the Aussie, regardless of what the RBA is doing. For your US-listed holdings (GOOGL, MSFT, TTWO), a stronger AUD means their value in Australian dollar terms is slightly reduced.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is Google dropping a brand new model called Gemini Omni — worth paying attention to as a GOOGL holder. Separately, Pope Leo has released a major document calling for strict global AI regulation, which is making waves as a signal that pressure on governments to rein in AI (and autonomous weapons in particular) is building from unexpected directions.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini Omni — a new all-in-one AI model
stories.why_it_matters: Google has announced Gemini Omni, described as a multimodal model — meaning it can handle text, images, audio, and video all in one go, rather than being limited to just one type of input. Details from the blog post are limited at this stage, but this is Google's direct answer to OpenAI's GPT-4o and signals they're continuing to invest heavily in AI capability. As a GOOGL shareholder, AI momentum is a core part of the bull case for Alphabet — this keeps them in the race.

stories.title: Pope Leo calls for tough global AI regulation and warns autonomous weapons are ungovernable
stories.why_it_matters: Pope Leo has published what's being described as a major manifesto on AI and humanity's future, calling for robust international regulation of artificial intelligence and specifically flagging that some autonomous weapons (AI-powered military systems that can make kill decisions without human input) have already reached a point where they're impossible for humans to meaningfully control. This is significant not because the Pope makes policy, but because it adds heavyweight moral authority to growing calls — from governments, academics, and now religious leaders — for binding global AI rules. Regulatory risk is one of the key uncertainties hanging over big AI investors like Google and Microsoft.

stories.title: Data privacy versus AI progress — the regulatory tightrope
stories.why_it_matters: A policy analysis piece exploring the tension between protecting personal data and allowing AI companies to train and improve their models. The core dilemma: AI gets better the more data it can access, but stricter privacy laws limit that access. No article text available for specific details, but this is the regulatory debate that will shape how companies like Google and Microsoft can operate in Europe and increasingly in Australia over the next few years.

sport.summary: The AFL world is in mourning today after the passing of Neale Daniher, one of the game's most beloved figures. In NRL, Round 13 injury news is rolling in ahead of this week's games, with the Warriors and Tigers both taking hits. And a World Surf League event in New Zealand was suspended after an Australian photographer was bitten — possibly by a shark.

stories.title: Neale Daniher passes away — AFL legend and MND advocate remembered
stories.why_it_matters: Neale Daniher, the former Melbourne Demons coach who became famous for his decade-long battle with MND (motor neurone disease) and his tireless fundraising through the Fight MND campaign, has passed away. He raised tens of millions of dollars for MND research and was one of the most respected figures in Australian sport. Garry Lyon led tributes today and has called on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to honour Daniher's legacy with meaningful support for MND research funding. A genuinely sad day for footy fans.

stories.title: NRL Round 13: Warriors and Tigers both hit by injury ahead of the week's games
stories.why_it_matters: Heading into Round 13, both the Warriors and Tigers are dealing with significant injury concerns. Fox Sports reports a Warriors hero has confirmed his season is over ('That's my footy done'), while there's also a twist involving Moses. The Tigers are also short on troops. Mystery surrounds which State of Origin stars will be released back to their clubs in time to play. Check the app for the full draw — the Titans play Sea Eagles on Saturday night.

stories.title: World Surf League event in New Zealand suspended after Australian photographer bitten by suspected shark
stories.why_it_matters: A World Surf League competition in New Zealand was put on hold after an Australian photographer was bitten while in the water — with authorities unsure whether it was a shark or a sea lion. The photographer was treated for injuries. The event was suspended as a precaution while the incident was investigated. No competitors were involved, but it's a dramatic interruption to the WSL tour.

watch_today.title: TTWO: Hold but watch closely — GTA 6 uncertainty is the risk
watch_today.detail: Take-Two dropped over 4% last night — that's a $10+ per share move in one session. The GTA 6 release is the company's entire story right now, and any hint of delay or pre-order news creates big swings. No bad fundamental news today, but this kind of volatility is worth watching. If you're uncomfortable with the ride, it's worth thinking about your position size. Hold for now unless an official delay is announced.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX: Hold — but oil's 5% drop overnight is a real headwind
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) fell nearly 5% last night to under $92 a barrel after OPEC cut its 2026 demand growth forecast. FUEL tracks global energy companies, so this directly drags on the fund. No need to panic — oil prices are still elevated historically — but if the oil price continues falling, expect FUEL to follow. Keep an eye on WTI crude this week.

watch_today.title: Labor's CGT and negative gearing changes — know what's coming
watch_today.detail: If you own investment property or assets with large capital gains (shares held a long time), Labor's proposed changes — cutting the CGT discount and tightening negative gearing on existing properties — matter to you. No legislation has passed yet, but Labor is signalling they're not backing down. Worth reviewing your tax position with your accountant before any changes are locked in.

watch_today.title: GOOGL: Gemini Omni launch is a green flag for the AI story
watch_today.detail: Google dropped Gemini Omni today — a new all-in-one AI model handling text, images, audio and video. GOOGL dipped 1.2% last night but that looks like general market noise rather than anything company-specific. The AI momentum story remains intact. Hold confidently.

watch_today.title: AUD strengthening — watch the impact on your US holdings
watch_today.detail: The Aussie dollar is up to 71.7 US cents and trending higher. A stronger AUD reduces the value of your US-listed holdings (GOOGL, MSFT, TTWO) and your VTS.AX ETF when converted back to Australian dollars. Nothing to act on today, but something to be aware of if the trend continues.
